newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's future leader arrives in Beijing for talks.
newsitem.headline: HK's future leader arrives in Beijing for talks.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa arrived in Beijing on Saturday to hold his first set of working-level talks with Chinese officials.
Tung made no statement on arrival.

He said earlier in Hong Kong that his one-day visit would focus on government funding and the legal status of the controversial post-colonial legislature which China will install when it resumes sovereignty of Hong Kong from Britain on July 1.

The 59-year-old former shipping magnate said he would discuss the constitutional status of the provisional legislature, which faces a legal challenge from Hong Kong's largest pro-democracy group, the Democratic Party.
Tung did not say, however, whether he would ask the Chinese parliament to pass a law to endorse the interim assembly to shield it against legal challenges.
The Democratic Party argues that it is illegal for two rival legislatures to sit simultaneously.
The provisional legislature, chosen under Beijing's supervision on December 21, is to reverse democratic reforms in the territory introduced by colonial governor Chris Patten.
The Democratic Party fared best in 1995 Legislative Council elections in Hong Kong but its deputies will lose their seats when Beijing dissolves the present elected chamber.

The trip is Tung's second to Beijing since his appointment as chief executive-designate on December 11. He was received by President Jiang Zemin, Premier Li Peng and Foreign Minister Qian Qichen during his first visit after his selection.
Tung is expected to return to Hong Kong on Sunday morning.
